chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
An 'Akulah' is not taken, and the 'Akulah' is the large/old one from the ewes among the sheep, nor its mother, nor the stallion ram.

key_terms.أَكُولَةٌ: A specific term referring to a large or old ewe, used in Zakat calculations.
key_terms.الْغَنَمِ: Sheep (specifically referring to sheep as distinct from camels or cattle in fiqh).
key_terms.الْفَحْلُ: The stallion ram (male sheep used for breeding).

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Akulah and which animals are excluded from Zakat on sheep?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the criteria for Zakat on sheep by excluding the 'Akulah'—a large, mature ewe—along with its mother and the male ram, ensuring the donor retains the most valuable breeding stock. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on fairness in charity, preventing the depletion of the owner's productive assets while fulfilling religious obligations.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘You do not take an Akoula, and the Akoula is the old one from the ewes which happens to be among the sheep, nor is parent, nor the stallion ram’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Uthman ibn ’Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,
’Akulah is not accepted. It is the great ewe among sheep, or the one that gives birth to it, as well as its breeder.’”
